candidates.source_attribution: Cyril of Alexandria, Commentary on Luke, Homily CI (R. Payne Smith trans., 1859). PD. Cf. Phil 2:8-9.

Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Luke (c. 430 AD)

On Christ's 'For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted' (Lk 14:11), Cyril reads the doubled-passive-formula (shall-be-abased + shall-be-exalted — the divine passive) as the canonical Lukan anchor of the great-reversal eschatological principle: God himself is the agent of both the abasement and the exaltation. The phrase recurs in Luke at 18:14 (Pharisee + Publican), making it a Lukan refrain. Tewahedo monastic spirituality cites Lk 14:11 + Lk 18:14 + Phil 2:8-9 (Christ's-own humiliation-and-exaltation) as the canonical triple-witness of the humility-precedes-exaltation pattern — the same pattern Christ embodies in the Incarnation.

Tewahedo monastic theology cites Lk 14:33 as the canonical Lukan anchor of the bahǝtawi's vow of poverty — the monastic outwardly enacts what every disciple inwardly possesses.
